newsitem.title: USA: CompUSA tops estimate with record Q3 income.
newsitem.headline: CompUSA tops estimate with record Q3 income.

text.p: Computer superstore retailer CompUSA Inc. said Wednesday it earned a record $32.7 million, or 35 cents a share, in its fiscal third quarter, benefitting from improved operating margins and higher sales.

CompUSA's profit for the period ended March 29 surpassed Wall Street analysts' mean estimate of 29 cents a share, as reported by First Call. CompUSA said it achieved a record 4 percent operating margin for the quarter.
Sales for the period increased to $1.27 billion, up from $1.07 billion last year. Profit for the third quarter of fiscal 1996 were $22.9 million, or 25 cents a share.
Comparable store sales were up 5.6 percent in the third quarter of fiscal 1997 for the 95 stores open one year or more.

"We are extremely pleased to report record earnings for our third quarter," James F. Halpin, CompUSA president and chief executive officer, said in a statement. "One of the highlights for the quarter was our achievement of a pretax operating margin over 4 percent -- a first for CompUSA."
CompUSA also said gross margins were 14.4 percent, the highest in its history.

CompUSA operates 124 computer superstores in 56 major markets throughout the United States, and PCs Compleat, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of CompUSA and a direct reseller of personal computers and peripherals.
